headline: Soft comps and restructuring charges squeeze profit
summary_short: Net sales rose 2.3% year over year to $4,541.3M, but a Petsense restructuring charge and VIP Petcare acquisition costs drove operating income down 19.2% to $467.1M and diluted EPS down 14.8% to $0.69.
summary_long: Net sales grew 2.3% y/y to $4,541.3M as new store openings offset a 1.5% comparable-sales decline driven by a weak May. Gross margin ticked up to 37.1% on cost discipline and tariff benefits, but SG&A jumped 14.4% on a $65.8M Petsense impairment/restructuring charge and $9.5M of VIP Petcare acquisition costs, pushing operating income down 19.2% to $467.1M and net income down 16.1% to $360.7M ($0.69 diluted EPS; adjusted $0.81). The company returned $260.9M to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Cash was $231.6M and long-term debt rose to $2,153.8M. FY2026 guidance was updated: net sales +2.5% to +3.5%, diluted EPS $1.78-$1.88 (adjusted $1.90-$2.00).

drivers.explanation: Positive April/June comps were more than offset by unusually adverse May conditions — seasonal and big-ticket softness plus lower discretionary spend — while consumables held up and companion animal lagged but improved through the quarter.
Net sales growth was driven by new store openings (28 Tractor Supply, 3 Petsense stores in the quarter), partially offset by a comparable store sales decline.

Improvement was primarily attributable to disciplined product cost management and tariff-related benefits that more than offset higher freight expense and price-investment spending; results include a $5.9M Petsense inventory write-down.

Decline was driven by a $65.8M Petsense impairment/restructuring charge and $9.5M of VIP Petcare acquisition costs, plus SG&A deleverage from lower comparable sales and higher medical-claims and legal-settlement expense.
Decline reflects the same Petsense and VIP Petcare charges flowing through operating income, partially offset by a lower effective tax rate of 19.8% versus 23.2% a year earlier.
